device.name: Booster T1 MotionTracking-v0 (Isaac Lab manager-based environment)

facts.text: Booster-T1-MotionTracking-v0 is registered with entry point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv, env_cfg_entry_point env_cfg.RoughWoStateEstimationEnvCfg, rsl_rl_cfg_entry_point ppo_cfg.PPORunnerCfg and the environment checker disabled

The registered T1 policy environment is RoughWoStateEstimationEnvCfg, which derives from FlatWoStateEstimationEnvCfg; that parent sets the policy motion_anchor_pos_b and base_lin_vel observation terms to None
FlatEnvCfg assigns the T1 robot configuration, the T1 action scale, the motion file t1_dance.npz, the trunk motion anchor and 18 tracked body names from the trunk to the ankles
The default T1 motion file is the bare relative name t1_dance.npz, not a path under booster_assets
TrackingEnvCfg is a ManagerBasedRLEnvCfg that groups the scene, observations, actions, commands, rewards, terminations, events and curriculum configuration
The environment uses decimation 4 over a 0.005 s simulation step and an episode length of 10.0 s, so one control step is 0.02 s and the time-out is 500 control steps
The sole action term is a joint-position action over every joint of the robot with the default joint positions as offset

The policy observation group concatenates the motion command, the motion anchor orientation matrix prefix, base angular velocity, joint position, joint velocity and the last action, in that order, with corruption enabled
The motion command is the concatenation of the reference joint positions and joint velocities loaded from the motion file

MotionLoader asserts that the motion file exists, loads it with numpy and reads fps, joint positions, joint velocities, body positions, orientations and linear and angular velocities, selecting the tracked bodies and joints by name
The T1 robot configuration spawns T1_23dof.urdf from the external booster_assets directory, so the 23-DoF robot description is not part of this clone
T1_CSV_JOINT_NAMES lists the 23 T1 joints in motion order: two head joints, four joints per arm, the waist yaw joint, four joints per leg and two ankle joints per leg
The T1 actuator groups cover the arms, waist, legs, feet and head, which are the joints the joint-position action term drives
The repository targets Isaac Lab 2.3.2 and Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and supports the T2, T1 and K1 platforms
booster_assets must be cloned and installed separately because it holds the Booster robot models and motion data
The package is installed in editable mode with python -m pip install -e source/booster_train
After training, deployment in MuJoCo or on real Booster robots is done in the separate booster_deploy repository
The training script launches the Omniverse app through AppLauncher(parser) before the environment is created
The training script creates the registered task with gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg), so the environment is driven through the Gymnasium make/step/reset interface

determinism.notes: the upstream environment draws its initial pose, velocity and joint-position randomization from the seeded simulator and the motion command term, and the motion file is fixed, so one seed and one action sequence are intended to repeat a trajectory on the same engine; this package's fake draws its reset state from Python's random.Random, so the same seed gives a different trajectory on the fake and upstream, and no upstream run was made

gaps: the deployed model is Isaac Sim/PhysX rigid-body dynamics with contacts (F1), but the fake backend is a pure Python analytic stand-in: it models no contacts, actuator forces, joint limits, sensors or contact or observation noise, and its numeric constants are placeholders, not the model's

one cap.world.step tick is one control step of 20 ms (the configuration's decimation 4 over the 0.005 s physics step); the physics step itself is 5 ms, and a client that needs it reads this note rather than timestep_ms, which names the step the bridge counts

the fake does not load the T1 URDF (downloaded with booster_assets, README.md:19-21, T1_23dof.urdf at booster_t1.py:25) or the t1_dance.npz motion file (a bare name at env_cfg.py:17): its 23-element action vector and 124-element flat observation are placeholder sizes, and the observation terms are zeros and an identity orientation rather than the configured MDP terms

the upstream policy observation group has six active terms after the T1 rough configuration disables motion_anchor_pos_b and base_lin_vel (env_cfg.py:42-46, tracking_env_cfg.py:119-134); the fake returns one flat float vector, while the upstream environment returns its observation groups as tensors

the fake models no reward term, no termination event and no time_out DoneTerm: it always returns a zero reward and terminated=False, and truncates at 500 control steps only because that follows from episode_length_s 10.0 and the 0.02 s control step

the action space is unbounded in this package because the clone states no action bound (the action scale of booster_t1.py:128-168 maps a unitless action to a joint target); the fake applies a placeholder gain instead of that scale and enforces the array length only
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware; the environment is trained in simulation and deployment is delegated to a separate repository (README.md:63)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the declared step only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the upstream environment was never constructed here (Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab and booster_assets are absent) and the fake was never compared with an upstream run

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
